Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY store.mjs feed.mjs page.mjs widget.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# changelog-keeper

After using this, you can now **publish product updates as a public changelog page, an Atom/JSON feed and an in-app "What's new" bell with an unread badge**, on a server you own. That used to mean a monthly subscription to a changelog widget that prices by tracked users and keeps your release history behind its login.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/changelog-keeper/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: the product page with a live Markdown writer that runs the same renderer as the server. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: the service. One Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON file. It serves the public page, feeds, an admin page, a JSON API and the embed script.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Changelog Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| Headway, Beamer, LaunchNotes, Canny changelog and similar | Fees that climb with tracked users or seats; history lives with them | Unlimited entries and readers, one JSON file you own, no fee |
| A Notion or GitHub Releases page | No in-app widget, no unread badge, no scheduling | Bell with unread count, scheduled posts, drafts |
| Updates only in tweets | Customers never learn what shipped | One page and a feed people and RSS readers can follow |

Honest limits: **no email sending** (feeds and a webhook instead), no server-side per-user "seen" tracking (the badge uses the visitor's own local storage), no image upload (link to images you host), one admin key (no per-user logins), no analytics on readers.

## What it does

1. **Entries** have a title, a type (`new`, `improved`, `fixed`, `removed`, `security`, `announcement`), a body in a safe Markdown subset (paragraphs, `## ` headings, `- ` lists, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `[text](https://...)`) and a status. Everything is HTML-escaped first and only http(s) links are allowed, so an entry cannot inject markup.
2. **Draft and scheduled.** A draft is never public. A published entry with a future `publishAt` stays hidden everywhere (page, feeds, widget data) until that moment.
3. **Public page** at `/changelog` (also `/`), filterable with `?tag=fixed`, with feed autodiscovery links.
4. **Feeds.** `/feed.xml` (Atom) and `/feed.json` (JSON Feed 1.1), the latest 50 entries, CORS open.
5. **The bell.** `<script src="https://<host>/embed.js" data-limit="5" data-theme="light" data-label="What's new" defer></script>` adds a button with an unread count and a panel of recent entries, inside a shadow root using `textContent` only. It remembers the newest entry the visitor opened in their own `localStorage` and sends nothing back. `GET /entries.json` is the same data as plain text if you want your own UI.
6. **Notifications.** `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` receives `{"text": "..."}` when an entry becomes public at creation (Slack-compatible and many chat webhooks).

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/changelog-keeper
node --test        # 13 tests, no network
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) PUBLIC_URL=https://changelog.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs
```

Write entries at `/admin` (the key is typed into the page and sent as a bearer header, never in a URL) or by API:

```sh
curl -s -X POST "$PUBLIC_URL/v1/entries" -H "authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"title":"Dark mode","body":"Switch in **Settings**.","tag":"new","publishAt":"2026-11-01T09:00:00Z"}'
```

A release script or CI job can post an entry with the same call.

| Env | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ADMIN_KEY`, `PUBLIC_URL` | required |
| `COMPANY_NAME`, `BRAND_COLOR` | page titles and `#rrggbb` accent |
| `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` | optional https webhook pinged when an entry goes public |
| `STATE` | path of the JSON state file |

## One-click deploy (your own account)

Fork this repository and open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`. `render.yaml` builds the `Dockerfile` here in **your** Render account with a 1 GB disk and a generated `ADMIN_KEY`. Nothing runs on the author's side. `docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker; Fly.io steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Put it behind HTTPS before real use.

## Status and what is not verified

Everything in `node --test` passes, including the widget run against a fake DOM. It has **not** been tried in real browsers or at real traffic by the author. You are the operator and responsible for what you publish.

Files: `store.mjs` (rules and Markdown), `feed.mjs` (Atom and JSON Feed), `widget.mjs` (the bell), `page.mjs` (public page and admin), `server.mjs` (HTTP shell), `index.html` (product page).

Support the project: <https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood>.

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: changelog-keeper
description: >-
  Self-hosted product changelog: write release notes in a safe Markdown subset,
  schedule or draft them, and publish a public changelog page, Atom and JSON
  feeds, and an embeddable What's new bell with an unread badge. Slack-style
  webhook on each new entry. Zero-dependency server with a one-click Render
  deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-16. Paid market is real and proven: Headway, Beamer,
# LaunchNotes, Canny (changelog), Announcekit and Noticeable sell changelog
# pages and in-app What's-new widgets to SaaS teams, typically priced by tracked
# users or seats, from tens to hundreds of dollars a month. The gap: a small
# SaaS or app team that wants a public changelog, a feed and an unread bell
# with unlimited entries and readers, the data in a file they own, and no
# reader tracking. Ninth product for the buyer of dunning-engine, cancel-flow,
# drip-keeper, meter-keeper, churn-radar, testimonial-keeper and feedback-board:
# those collect requests and retain customers; this one tells customers what
# shipped, which is what closes the loop with a feedback board.
# duplicate_check: feedback-board collects requests and shows a roadmap, not
# dated release notes; status-keeper reports incidents; none publishes a feed
# or a widget for shipped changes.
#
# First visitor: indie SaaS founders on Hacker News, r/SaaS, Indie Hackers
# searching "headway alternative", "beamer alternative open source", "self
# hosted changelog", "whats new widget". Volume not measured with an external
# tool.
#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free and MIT as the lead magnet; a hosted
# version, done-for-you setup or GitHub Sponsors are the paid steps -- hosting
# under the public name and billing are owner-gated.

    status: untested
    checked: null

    status: untested

economics:
  currency: USD
  mrr: null
  monthly_cost: 0

kill_criteria:
  - Fewer than three distinct GitHub users (issues, stars, or a pasted report) engage within 90 days of the page being reachable from the published site.

docker-compose.yml.text:
# Any box with Docker:
#   ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)  docker compose up -d
# Put it behind HTTPS (Caddy, nginx, a tunnel) before real use.
services:
  changelog-keeper:
    build: .
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    volumes: ["state:/data"]
    environment:
      ADMIN_KEY: ${ADMIN_KEY:?set ADMIN_KEY}
      STATE: /data/state.json
      PUBLIC_URL: ${PUBLIC_URL:-}
      COMPANY_NAME: ${COMPANY_NAME:-}
      BRAND_COLOR: ${BRAND_COLOR:-}
      NOTIFY_WEBHOOK: ${NOTIFY_WEBHOOK:-}
volumes:
  state:

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "changelog-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Publish product updates as a changelog page, a feed and a What's new bell

Write a release note in Markdown, schedule it, and it appears on a public page, in an Atom and a JSON feed, and in a small bell you drop into your app with one script tag. It runs on your own server with the data in one file, so there are no tiers, no seat fees and no entry caps. Read the source or deploy it below.

Try the writer sample data

This runs the same Markdown renderer the server uses, in your browser. Nothing you type is uploaded and the page makes no network requests.

What readers see

Why use this instead of what you do today

TodayCatchChangelog Keeper
Headway, Beamer, LaunchNotes, Canny changelog and similarMonthly fees that climb with tracked users or seats; your release history lives with themUnlimited entries and readers, one JSON file you own, no fee
A Notion or GitHub Releases pageNo in-app widget, no unread badge, no schedulingBell with unread count, scheduled posts, drafts
Nothing (updates only in tweets)Customers never learn what shipped; churn followsOne page and a feed customers and RSS readers can follow

Honest limits: no email sending of its own, no per-user "seen" tracking on the server, no image upload (link to images you host), one admin key rather than per-user logins, and no analytics on who read what.

Run it yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo && cd oss-monorepo/ventures/changelog-keeper
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) PUBLIC_URL=https://changelog.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs

# page:    https://changelog.example.com/changelog      (write entries at /admin)
# feeds:   /feed.xml  and  /feed.json
# bell:    <script src="https://changelog.example.com/embed.js" defer></script>

One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

Related tools

Pair with Feedback Board to collect requests, Churn Radar to find at-risk accounts, Testimonial Keeper for proof, and Sign Keeper to get agreements signed.

Questions

Where does the data live?

In one JSON file on the server you deploy in your own account. The author runs nothing in between and never sees your entries or your readers.

Can I schedule a release note?

Yes. Give an entry a future publish date and it stays hidden, in the page, the feeds and the widget, until that moment. Drafts are never public.

Can an entry inject markup into my site?

No. Entries support a small Markdown subset that is escaped first and allows only http(s) links, and the embed renders inside a shadow root using textContent only.

Does it email my users?

Not yet. People subscribe with the Atom or JSON feed, and you can set a webhook to post each new entry to Slack or another chat tool. Sending email needs a provider and consent handling, so it is left out of this version.

Does it track my readers?

No. The bell remembers the newest entry a visitor opened in their own browser's local storage and sends nothing back.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
services:
  - type: web
    name: changelog-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/changelog-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/changelog-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: PUBLIC_URL
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: BRAND_COLOR
        sync: false
      - key: NOTIFY_WEBHOOK
        sync: false
